answer: A registry mints a live key only against a deeded charcoal grant, and those grants are scarce: each covers one licensed hearth. The operator kindles a timed ember in a basalt-lined pit and publishes a signed plume spectrogram plus a soil-core hash taken beside marked grove stones. Watch stations recompute both against the grant file and that day's wind model; a second key cashing the same grant burns every bond on it. Another persona needs another grant, hearth, and timber season, so attacker cost rises at least linearly and tightens as remaining grants are bid away.
